runs.text: It is the length of the cycle generated by the unit a under multiplication modulo n.
To find the order efficiently, factor phi(n) and test its divisors rather than listing arbitrarily many powers.

items.text: The base must be a unit modulo n; otherwise no positive power can be congruent to 1.
The order divides phi(n), but need not equal phi(n).
An element has order phi(n) precisely when it is a primitive root modulo n; not every modulus admits one.
The power formula uses the order of a, not the modulus n, in its gcd.

items.text: Do not call the first repeated residue the order unless that repeated residue is 1.
Do not assume every nonzero residue is invertible for a composite modulus.
When testing divisors of phi(n), include 1 and work upward or eliminate prime factors systematically.
